terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive
terms.comment: In conversation an assumption is simply what one believes or thinks: crēdō, putō (see believe, think).

terms.gloss: take it (that), lay down as given
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. Brut. 165: pōnō satis in eō fuisse ōrātiōnis atque ingenī
Cic. Div. 1.118: hōc autem positō atque concessō
terms.comment: Hōc positō: on this assumption. The imperative pōne, “suppose”, is late (Ambrose: Lewis & Short); for “suppose that …” see suppose.

terms.gloss: assume, take as granted (in an argument)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. N.D. 1.89: beātōs esse deōs sūmpsistī

terms.gloss: take for granted, regard as certain

phrases.latin: cōnscrīpsī epistulam noctū; nec ille ad mē rediit; oblītum crēdidī.
phrases.english: I wrote the letter during the night; he never came back for it; I assumed he had forgotten.
You assumed that the gods are happy: we grant it.

phrases.latin: tamen pōnō satis in eō fuisse ōrātiōnis atque ingenī
phrases.english: yet I take it that he had eloquence and talent enough
